title: Signal cartography & dashboard indexing (working draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working notebook for mapping observability signals (metrics + traces) to product-level user journeys and then indexing dashboards/widgets by persona, severity, and query-cost. Goal: reduce cognitive load when debugging inference regressions and make it obvious where to look for a given symptom (latency, cost regression, degradation, fallback, hallucination signal).

Scope:
- Whole inference pipeline: ingress -> routing -> runtime -> kv-cache -> model exec -> postprocess -> responses
- Both hosted and dedicated/private variants (tags for tenant vs global)
- Focus on operational signals (SLO, error, cost) and developer signals (model-quality, rerank signals)

Quick glossary (working):
- Signal cartography: mapping a user-observed symptom to the smallest set of signals + dashboards needed to root-cause
- Anchor metric: the one metric we use to trigger an investigation (e.g., per_route.request_latency.p95)
- Trace anchor: span-level breadcrumb that ties distributed work to a session/request id

Anchor metrics (candidate list) — short defs and useful tags:
- inference.request.count: total requests (tag: route, model_version, region, customer_tier)
- inference.tokens.per_request.p50/p95: tokens emitted per request (useful for cost regressions)
- per_route.latency.ms.p50/p95/p99: end-to-end latency from request receive -> response end (tags: route, model_variant, cpu/gpu)
- kv_cache.hit_ratio: prefix cache hits / accesses (tags: model_version, cache_ttl, prefix_len_bucket)
- routing.fallback.count: counts where primary model unavailable and fallback chosen (tags: fallback_reason, region)
- runtime.batch_utilization.p50: % of batch slots used per iteration (helps diagnose throughput regressions)
- model.variant_switches.rate: frequency of model swaps during rollout (A/B/canary)
- capacity.spillover.count: number of requests spilled to lower tier due to capacity constraints

Tracing anchors & span conventions (proposal):
- Root span name: "request.inference"
  - attributes: request.id, route, model_version, customer_id (hashed), is_canary
- Child spans: "ingest.http", "routing.policy", "runtime.exec", "kv_cache.lookup", "runtime.batch.wait", "runtime.kv.apply", "postprocess.format"
- Each token-generation should not create a separate global span (too high-cardinality). Instead, emit periodic "token-batch" spans (one per kernel step) with attributes: seq_start, seq_end, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_frac
- Error spans must contain error.kind and sampled_stack (if available), plus trace severity label (sev=warn|error|fatal)

Dashboard indexing model (how to organize):
- Primary axis: symptom -> persona -> cost
  - Symptom: latency / error / cost / quality / routing
  - Persona: SRE / Runtime eng / Product ML / Solutions eng / CS
  - Cost: estimated query cost (cheap/medium/expensive) to guide where to run real-time queries vs offline
- Each dashboard must have: "Investigate this" section (breadcrumbs), and a one-line intent (e.g., "diagnose routing throttles for p95 spikes")
- Dashboard tags: persona, symptom, severity_tier (P0/P1/P2), estimated_query_cost, retention_window

Widget catalog & retention heuristics (notes):
- High-cardinality raw tables: keep for 7d, accessible by analysts (not on default dashboards)
- Aggregated sparklines (route-level p95): keep for 90d on SRE landing dashboard
- Heavy sample traces (full span payload): keep for 30d but only with severity-weighted sampling (see sampling below)

Sampling and trace budget rules (practical):
- Error-first sampling: 100% traces when error=true for 7d window, then sampled 10% afterwards
- Severity-weighted reservoir: weight traces by latency bucket * error_flag to prioritize high-latency errors
- Session-level sampling: for long-running multi-step sessions, sample first trace and then 1/n to limit noise
- Cost cap: per-customer trace ingestion cap to protect backend; surface caps as "trace-limited" on dashboards

PromQL-ish example queries (illustrative):
- p95 latency for route X
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(per_route_latency_bucket{route="/chat"}[5m])) by (le))
- kv cache hit ratio
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
- batch utilization
  - avg_over_time(runtime_batch_utilization{pool="inference"}[5m])

Investigation playbook (short):
1) Start with anchor metric + timeline (p95 spike window)
2) Check per-route breakdown, region, and customer_tier funnels
3) Look for routing.fallback.count spikes -> inspect routing.policy spans in sampled traces
4) Check runtime.exec duration distribution and runtime.batch.wait (are we waiting for sparse requests?)
5) Inspect kv_cache.hit_ratio and prefix_len_bucket distribution (cache thrash?). If kv cache miss rate increased alongside tokens/request, likely prefix-shift regression
6) If model.variant_switches.rate > 0 around window, check rollout config and telemetry for quantized fallback events
7) If no infra signal, collect a small set of sampled traces (severity-weighted) and attach to the incident

Instrumentation checklist (for new metrics/spans):
- Metric name follows dot-delimited namespace: inference.<subsystem>.<signal>
- Labels: route, model_version, model_variant, region, cluster_id, customer_tier, sample_rate
- Buckets: use standard latency buckets + an overflow bucket for huge pauses > 30s
- Traces: ensure request.id is present and injected into downstream pods via header X-RW-Req-Id
- Low-overhead: metrics must be emitted at aggregation-friendly cardinality; prefer route/model_version coarser tags where possible

Open questions / trade-offs:
- token-level tracing vs batch-level: do we need token spans for debugging hallucinations? cost vs value unclear
- Default persona dashboards: how many landing dashboards before we cause navigation paralysis for SREs?
- Should routing.fallback be a sampled event with detailed reasons stored in long-term DB rather than traces to reduce trace volume?

Next actions / owners:
- Markus: prototype dashboard index page (per persona filters) — RFC due 2024-11-12 (INF-2345)
- Priya: implement kv_cache metrics (prefix_len_bucket) + add to demo dashboard — PR link in artifacts
- Tomoko: finalize trace sampling policy and add to agent policy docs (compliance check)

Notes to self (fast brain-dump):
- Keep SLO anchors minimal — too many SLOs = no signal. Stick to global-request-p95, per-route-p95, kv_cache_hit_ratio, & error-rate
- Consider "investigate-mode" flag in console that switches dashboards to pre-filtered timeframe and tenant context

References:
- INF-2345 (tracking prototype)
